strings.intro.narration.arrival: It's the night before the Mid-Autumn Festival, and lanterns hang all along Kwai Heung Street. {player_name} has barely turned the corner when the news breaks: the street's pride and joy, the giant rabbit lantern, has vanished into thin air.
strings.intro.line.granny_greeting: So you're the detective? Good, good. I built that rabbit with my own two hands, every strip of bamboo, every sheet of paper, and it has seen this street through forty Mid-Autumns. As for the thief, mark my words: his luck is as short as a rabbit's tail.
strings.intro.line.kit_joke: Chill, Granny! That rabbit's bigger than my bike. Who's gonna nick it? Unless it did a runner, back to the moon to spend the festival with Chang'e.
strings.intro.choice.ask: Ask at the cha chaan teng
strings.intro.ending.a: The scraps of coloured paper lead you up to the rooftop. And there it is: the rabbit lantern, safe and sound, a fresh patch on its torn ear. Kit had smuggled it up here to mend it, a secret surprise for Granny.
strings.intro.ending.b: The owner carries on polishing a glass. "The rabbit? Just left on the back of Kit's motorbike. Wearing a helmet, no less." You dash outside, just in time to see a giant rabbit's head bobbing away into the traffic...
strings.voice.line.granny_scold: Kit, my boy, late again! Seven o'clock, you promised, and it's gone half past. A promise is a debt, young man. Do you understand me?
strings.voice.line.kit_excuse: Granny, so unfair! Orders were off the charts tonight. I was going so fast I nearly took off for the moon. And not one double-yolk mooncake got squashed. You should be thanking me!
strings.voice.line.granny_tease: Hmph. That mouth of yours is faster than your bike. You young people spend all day hunched over your phones, 'checking in' here and there, and not one of you can make a lantern. Each generation is worse than the last.
strings.voice.line.kit_soft: So I'll learn. Go on, Granny, teach me. Your lanterns are proper old school, but they've got soul. I mean it.
strings.voice.ending.a: Granny grumbles that Kit is all thumbs, yet her hands never stop as she guides his, strip by strip, through the shape of a rabbit's ear. By midnight a small rabbit lantern sits on the table, its head tilted just a little.
strings.voice.ending.b: Kit leaps onto his motorbike and shouts over his shoulder, "Granny, I'll carry your lantern tomorrow. Free of charge!" Granny waves him away. "Off you go, then. Mind the road, and don't go running off like that rabbit."
strings.pun.line.king_intro: Well, well, {player_name}! You seek the rabbit lantern? Then first you must get past me! Guess right and a prize is yours. Guess wrong, and I shall be over the moon!
strings.pun.line.king_riddle: Hear my riddle: "Snip the tail off a bunny, and you'll have something to eat." What word is left?
strings.pun.choice.answer: A bun! A bunny without its tail!
strings.pun.choice.mooncake: Mooncake! It must be a mooncake!
strings.pun.ending.a: The Riddle King strokes his beard and roars with laughter. "Splendid! And since buns are on the house tonight, so is your clue: the lantern will come to light, but only to those who wait. When the moon climbs above the archway, the rabbit will show itself."
strings.pun.ending.b: The Riddle King doubles over, howling with laughter. "A mooncake? You're so hungry your brain has turned to lotus paste! Double yolk, is it? Then that's your score: a double duck!"
strings.ui.hud.toast:
New clue!
{player_name} found rabbit fur by the archway.
strings.ui.ending.a: You raise the {item_name} and aim it at the archway. A giant rabbit's shadow leaps up the wall. The lantern must be close!
strings.ui.ending.b: You snap your bag shut and sit down to munch a mooncake. Then Kit's voice floats up the street: "Oi, {player_name}! Over here! I've found the rabbit!"
